title: Turing bifurcation, criticality, and multistability in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation
authors: Yui Nagayama, Masaharu Nagayama, Hiroshi Ishii
abstract: This paper considers a nonlocal advection--reaction--diffusion equation with logistic growth. We investigate how the interaction kernel affects the criticality of Turing bifurcations and the associated multistability. We first prove that nonhomogeneous stationary solutions bifurcate from the positive homogeneous stationary solution. Center manifold reduction yields an amplitude equation near the bifurcation point. This equation provides criteria for supercritical and subcritical bifurcations in terms of the Fourier transform of the interaction kernel. We also derive a sufficient condition for subcriticality. This condition can be satisfied by sufficiently localized attractive interactions. Based on these analytical results, we investigate multistability through numerical bifurcation analysis. The numerical results show that the stable homogeneous stationary solution can coexist with stable nonhomogeneous stationary solutions or stable time-periodic solutions.
summary: This paper analyzes pattern formation in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation by studying Turing bifurcations. It uses advanced mathematical techniques, including center manifold reduction, to determine the criticality of the bifurcation based on the interaction kernel. The findings demonstrate that the system can exhibit complex multistability involving stable stationary and time-periodic patterns.
main_problem: The paper investigates the relationship between the properties of the interaction kernel and the criticality of Turing bifurcations in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation.
main_result: The analysis establishes criteria based on the amplitude equation's cubic coefficient to determine if the bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical, confirming the possibility of multistability.
method: The study employs linear stability analysis, center manifold reduction to derive an amplitude equation, and numerical bifurcation analysis.
model_or_system: The model is a nonlocal advection–reaction–diffusion equation with logistic growth, posed on a finite interval with periodic boundary conditions.
key_observables: Turing bifurcation point, existence of nonhomogeneous stationary solutions, and the co-existence of stable homogeneous, nonhomogeneous stationary, or time-periodic solutions.
important_parameters: The diffusion coefficient ($d$), growth rate ($c$), and the properties of the interaction kernel ($K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the spectrum of the linearized operator crosses zero only at a single mode ($n=N$) at the bifurcation point.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the stationary problem using Fourier series and linear operators, applying the Crandall–Rabinowitz theorem to prove local existence of bifurcating solutions, deriving a reduced amplitude equation via center manifold reduction, and finally using numerical methods to confirm multistability.
why_interesting: While the model is classical PDE-based, the study of pattern formation, stability, and phase transitions (like Turing bifurcations) in reaction-diffusion systems is a core topic in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

Figure 2 shows bifurcation diagrams for three values of β. Representative solutions and their time evolution are shown in Figure 3. We choose the parameters so that the first Fourier mode is the critical mode when the homogeneous stationary solution first loses stability. For β = 0.15 (Figure 2 A), the bifurcation is supercritical. In contrast, for smaller values of β, the bifurcation becomes subcritical, and two different bifurcation structures are observed (Figure 2 B–C).
